glosses: An apparently self-contradictory statement, which can only be true if it is false, and vice versa.

examples.text: "This sentence is false" is a paradox.
The active sense of living which we all enjoy, before reflection shatters our instinctive world for us, is self-luminous and suggests no paradoxes.

glosses: A counterintuitive conclusion or outcome.

examples.text: It is an interesting paradox that drinking a lot of water can often make you feel thirsty.

glosses: A claim that two apparently contradictory ideas are true.

examples.text: Not having a fashion is a fashion; that's a paradox.

glosses: A thing involving contradictory yet interrelated elements that exist simultaneously and persist over time.
A person or thing having contradictory properties.

examples.text: He is a paradox; you would not expect him in that political party.

glosses: An unanswerable question or difficult puzzle, particularly one which leads to a deeper truth.

examples.text: And only by dismantling our preconceptions of age can we be free to understand the paradox: How young are the old?

L’humanité est actuellement dans un étrange paradoxe, d’un côté elle est obsédée par la sécurité et l’augmentation de l’espérance de vie et de l’autre, elle détruit son environnement et en particulier le sol nourricier, mettant ainsi en péril sa propre survie.
